independence: Read font manifest and generated my own HarfBuzz/FreeType Russian proofs. Did not read prior reports, matrices, other reviewer reports, or their proof images/scripts. Source/font were not modified.

tests.renderer: HarfBuzz shaping + FreeType grayscale rasterization; black on white, pixel-size-matched opsz

ui.reason: Regular 400 Russian labels at 12–20 px remain legible with matched opsz. Thin 100 at 12–16 px has very low stroke coverage; heavy 900 is usable for short emphasis, not a default text weight.

headings.reason: At 24–96 px the tested Cyrillic constructions and diacritics remain recognizable at 100, 400 and 900; no visible broken joins or counter collapse in the inspected samples.

body.reason: Russian paragraphs at 14 and 18 px / weight 400 are readable and have coherent texture. This is a short visual inspection, not a reading study.

sustained_reading.reason: Four-line paragraphs do not establish long-session readability or fatigue; no human reading test was performed.

findings.condition: U+2022 BULLET in the heading test shapes to glyph 0 at all three weights. Rendered as an outlined oval unrelated to surrounding weight. All requested Cyrillic letters shape to nonzero glyph IDs.
findings.recommendation: Add U+2022 with an appropriate bullet drawing/advance, or require an explicit fallback before claiming general editorial punctuation coverage.
findings.acceptance_test: Shape RU text containing U+2022 at 100/400/900 and opsz 14/48; require nonzero glyph ID and visually appropriate bullet at each instance.

findings.condition: At 12–16 px, weight 100 renders Russian UI strokes very faint; at weight 900 the same sizes produce dense counters. No Cyrillic-specific failure isolated.
findings.recommendation: Use weight 400 for default UI/body; reserve extremes for large display or deliberate emphasis. Do not redesign Cyrillic solely from the extreme samples.
findings.acceptance_test: Check 12/14/16 px Russian labels at the intended default weight in target native/browser rasterizers on actual displays.

limitations: Single renderer, grayscale rasterization; no CoreText/browser screenshot comparison.
Three weights and sampled optical sizes, not exhaustive continuous-axis testing.
Short excerpts only, no controlled human sustained-reading study.
No Latin benchmark or competitor comparison used.
Visual taste is not treated as a construction failure: flat-top Д/Л and angular ж/к are stylistic choices.
